bijection.conclusion: witness_commitment <-> (12 syndrome residues, 6 account_projection residues) is a bijection on canonical inputs for fixed (pad_seed, slot_id). Therefore a LEAF-FIXED commitment fixes ALL 18 residues, hence the account_projection (the 6-lane witness opening) is UNIQUELY determined.

repack_is_tautology.conclusion: repack is an algebraic identity (masked = (masked-mask)+mask); it adds no independent constraint. The binding power is entirely that the leaf FIXES account_witness_commitment, which fixes all 18 residues.

residual.only_remaining_attack: SHA256 collision on the opening_commitment frame or the witness_opening_digest frame -- this is the named `prevalidation_leaf_binding_break` / `qrom_or_domain_separation_break`, NOT an algebraic creation-time survivor
residual.witness_free_assignment: impossible: account_projection is read out of the fixed commitment; exactly one opening per leaf

spend_survivor_under_creation.conclusion: The two spend-only survivor witnesses map to TWO DISTINCT opening_commitments. The leaf fixes exactly ONE opening_commitment. So at most ONE of {w_a, w_b} can satisfy a given leaf. The spend-only two-witnesses survivor is KILLED at creation time: it required the account_witness_commitment to move freely, but the leaf pins it.

verdict: NO creation-time algebraic survivor: the masked_state18 repack-to-LEAF-FIXED-commitment makes the account-witness opening map injective. The spend-only two-witnesses survivor is killed because the leaf pins a single account_witness_commitment and the 18-residue packing is a bijection. The binding reduces to SHA256 collision resistance (a named break), not an open algebraic gap.
